title: Peering inside plants
question: How did people work out what plants are made of?
hook: It took microscopes, fossils and a few strong arguments to see inside a plant.
idea: Plant anatomy grew from describing structure into the study of plant cells and tissues.

beats.prompt: Put these works in order, earliest first.
Match each botanist to what he or she did.
pairs: Described the mitotic process in plant cells
Described the structures of fossilized plants
beats.explain: Each added a different layer to what is known about plant structure.

beats.prompt: In 1838 Matthias Schleiden compared lower plants with higher plants. What did he state?

choices.label: Both kinds are made of a single cell
choices.feedback: That fits only the lower plants.

choices.label: Lower plants are one cell; higher plants are many cells
Higher plants are one cell; lower plants are many cells
choices.feedback: This reverses it: the simpler plants are the single-celled ones.

choices.label: Neither kind is made of cells
choices.feedback: Plant cells had been recognized since Grew.

beats.explain: Schleiden stated that the lower plants all consist of one cell, while the higher plants are composed of many individual cells.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: Plant anatomy originally included morphology, the description of a plant's outward form.
Since the mid-20th century the field has been treated as separate, covering only internal structure.
So describing a flower's outward shape counts as plant anatomy today.
Anatomy is now often studied at the cellular level, using sectioned tissue and microscopy.
beats.explain: Outward form belongs to morphology, which the field has not included since the mid-20th century.
